title: 0319-leicesters-tale-another-perspective-on-the
universal_lens: The core primitive is the Poisson Match Simulation (PMS) operator, which maps observed shot-based expected-goal (xG) performance to probabilistic projections of final league tables, points accumulation, and relegation risk. The methodological duality lies between the "base" distance-zone model and the more complex "interaction" model that includes ball-control effects. Failure occurs when the model treats exceptional goal-scoring efficiency as pure variance rather than skill, leading to inflated probability estimates for extreme outcomes such as championship titles.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, this corresponds to a conformal predictive system that uses historical shot data to construct empirical quantiles of team performance. The PMS operator provides a non-parametric bootstrap distribution for end-of-season points, enabling the calculation of exact exceedance probabilities for Top 4 qualification or relegation. The "ex ante" mode serves as an early warning indicator of league structure instability.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the primitive maps to a state-transition model where each quarter represents a Markov state defined by first-half xG performance. The transition kernel encodes the probability of moving to higher or lower ranks based on residualized performance. The "interaction" model captures strategic adjustments in possession-based attacking and defending, analogous to EPA-weighted play sequences.

primitives.name: Poisson Match Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions Paper's stated equations, copied faithfully: (1) xG_{team, match} = Σ_{i=1}^{N} p_i, where N = shots by the team in the match, p_i = P(shot i is a goal).
primitives.latex: xG_{team, match} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i, \quad p_i = \text{P(shot } i \text{ is a goal)}
primitives.assumptions: Independent Poisson scoring; no memory of previous goals; equal opportunity across shots; constant quality of chance within categories.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Large sample limit N→∞ recovers deterministic xG; small N leads to overdispersion and heavy tails in goal counts.

layer2.mapping: Maps to NFL Expected Points Added (EPA) per drive, where each play contributes a state-value change. Monte Carlo simulation of remaining drives yields distribution of final game score differential.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between simulated and actual goal differences, rank distributions across replications.
